newsitem.title: USA: U.S. wheat gluten group files petition against EU.
newsitem.headline: U.S. wheat gluten group files petition against EU.

text.p: The U.S. Wheat Gluten Industry Council (WGIC) said it filed a special petition Wednesday asking the U.S. Trade Representative to investigate European Union subsidies and other trading practices that it said damage the U.S. wheat gluten industry.

Ladd Seaberg, president of the WGIC and chief executive officer of Midwest Grain Products, a leading U.S. wheat gluten producer, told Reuters the WGIC filed the petition because efforts to negotiate with the European Union over the last two years had failed.
"Quite frankly, the Europeans have taken the position to stall, stall, stall, and so we felt imperative at this time to proceed with...a legal stance to put pressure on the situation," Seaberg said.
The WGIC's petition, filed under Section 301 of the Tariff Act of 1974, calls for an international panel of the World Trade Organization to examine the EU trading practices.
The WGIC said the petition, filed with the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative, should ultimately allow the United States to retaliate against the European Union if the practices do not stop.

The WGIC said the EU uses excessively high tariff barriers that prohibit other countries from exporting wheat gluten to Europe, and that EU subsidies directly violate provisions of the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade.

"The EU has been manipulating the costs of raw materials and finished products so as to flood the world market with European wheat gluten and its co-product, wheat starch," the WGIC said in a statement.
Wheat gluten is the natural protein portion of wheat that is extracted after wheat is milled into flour.
The WGIC said that over the past three years, European wheat gluten producers have doubled their share of the U.S. market, jumping to 27.7 percent from 13.7 percent.
